messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 — SylphCorp (private VPC) reporting model-serving errors. Alerts: NLB target health flapping, API 503s for tenant pool. Paging on-call. @matt (oncall) please ack and start triage. :rotating_light:

matt (oncall): acked. I'm on it. quick summary? customer impact?

anna_cs: i just heard from Sylph support channel — they're seeing 20-40% of requests 503-ing since ~09:05 UTC. Customer reported a recent security-group update they pushed around 08:55.

matt (oncall): ok — likely candidate. tagging neteng and infra. @sarah_neteng @devin_infra can you run NLB/healthcheck checks and confirm if targets are failing from our probe IPs?

sarah_neteng: looking. pulled NLB target health via AWS (using the customer's AWS read-only role). output snippet: ```
$ aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:123:tg/abc
{
  "TargetHealthDescriptions": [
    { "Target": {"Id": "10.3.4.12", "Port": 8080}, "TargetHealth": {"State": "unhealthy", "Description": "Connection timed out"}},
    { "Target": {"Id": "10.3.4.13", "Port": 8080}, "TargetHealth": {"State": "healthy", "Description": ""}}
  ]
}
```

sarah_neteng: healthchecks are intermittently timing out from our health nodes (us-west-2 probes). looking at VPC flow logs for the ENI that talks to 10.3.4.12 — I see DENY on outbound ports 1024-65535 to our probe IPs.

devin_infra: can we repro from inside their VPC quickly? asking customer to run a quick curl from a bastion to the worker IPs. sylph-eng, can you run these and paste results? `curl -vS --max-time 5 http://10.3.4.12:8080/health`

sylph-eng: running now — paste: ```
$ curl -vS --max-time 5 http://10.3.4.12:8080/health
* Connected to 10.3.4.12 (10.3.4.12) port 8080 (#0)
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: 10.3.4.12
>
< HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
< content-type: application/json
< content-length: 45

{"status":"degraded","reason":"upstream unreachable"}
* Connection #0 to host 10.3.4.12 left intact
```

sylph-eng: also tried from a different subnet -> sometimes 200, sometimes 503. we just added a deny-all-egress rule on the worker SG to tighten outbound earlier (we thought workers don't need wide outbound).

matt (oncall): that matches. NLB healthcheck traffic originates from ephemeral source ports; deny-all-egress is impacting replies. plan: ask customer to relax SG outbound to allow reply to our healthcheck source IP ranges OR temporarily allow outbound to 10.3.4.0/24 -> ports 1024-65535 to permit healthcheck handshake.

anna_cs: paging customer SRE now to request quick rollback of the deny-all-egress or add explicit allow for our probe ranges. Sylph contact says they'll try a quick rule change. ETA 10 minutes.

tim_product: product note — this is only for the private VPC tenant pool for Sylph, no global model degradation, but traffic rerouted inside their pool is causing quota hits; we should monitor cost/throughput implications if we reprovision fallback.

devin_infra: alternative mitigation (if customer cannot change SG soon): we can failover the tenant to their dedicated standby pool in another AZ (needs manual approval). That will cause brief DNS TTL miss; we should coordinate with CS before doing. Also we can switch NLB healthcheck protocol to TCP-only temporarily, but that requires customer consent and may not help if replies are blocked.

sarah_neteng: adding concrete diagnostic commands for the customer to run (ask them to paste output): ```
# from their bastion or worker subnet
nc -vz 10.3.4.12 8080 || true
curl -vS http://10.3.4.12:8080/health || true
# check iptables/nft rules on worker if self-managed
sudo iptables -S | head -n 200 || sudo nft list ruleset || true
# VPC flow logs quick filter (if they can query):
filter: dstAddr=PROBE_IP and dstPort=XXXX and action=REJECT
```

sylph-eng: we've applied a temporary allow rule: outbound allow to 10.3.4.0/24 port 1024-65535 from worker-sg. testing now.

sylph-eng: after change curl -> ```
$ curl -vS --max-time 5 http://10.3.4.12:8080/health
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"status":"ok"}
```

sarah_neteng: rechecked target health via AWS API — all targets now show State: healthy. propagation within ALB/NLB shows green.

incident-bot: Incident update — severity reduced to P2 (partial customer service degradation mitigated). Please confirm with customer that they will make a durable SG change (whitelist Redwood probe ranges or adjust egress policy) and file a postmortem.

anna_cs: Sylph will open a change ticket to add a more restrictive rule that allows our probe ranges only and will revert deny-all. they also want recommendations — @sarah_neteng can you paste the probe CIDRs and a short note?

sarah_neteng: probe CIDRs: 35.198.12.0/24 and 35.199.18.0/24 (these are the healthcheck ranges we asked them to allow). recommendation: allow outbound ephemeral replies to those CIDRs OR add a stateful ALLOW for established connections on ephemeral ports. also remind them to test template changes in staging.

matt (oncall): thanks everyone — I'll stay on for the next 10m to watch metrics. Anna please book a short follow-up call with Sylph SRE to walk through the change. If healthchecks regress, we'll consider rerouting to standby pool.

anna_cs: scheduled 30m runbook review with Sylph SRE.

tim_product: tagging for post-incident follow-up: we should add a doc to the private VPC onboarding checklist that calls out the need to avoid deny-all-egress on worker SGs (or provide explicit rules to whitelist our probe ranges).

devin_infra: ops note: documented runbook step to validate NLB health via `aws elbv2 describe-target-health` and to ask for `curl` from customer bastion. I'll add a short snippet to the internal runbook.

incident-bot: Incident resolved for now — monitors green for 8 minutes. If regressions occur reopen thread or @matt (oncall) will escalate. :white_check_mark:
